# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
**Travel Trade Statistics**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Privacy
The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions.

The International Trade Administration’s National Travel and Tourism Office (NTTO) has updated its U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor, a data visualization tool highlighting overseas visitation to U.S. states and cities through interactive tables and maps, to calendar year 2024. Highlights for 2024 include:
*   Top state visited by overseas visitors: New York (9,802,000)  
*   Top city-MSA visited by overseas visitors: New York City (9,525,000)  
*   Biggest state # gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Florida (+927,000)  
*   Biggest % gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Vermont (+87.8%)  
*   Top 5 states’ combined market share: 62.0% of overseas visitors  
*   Top 5 city-MSA’s combined market share: 48.5% of overseas visitors
**U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor** has six sections:
*   **Top 5 States and U.S. Cities in 2024**: volume, gains and declines  
*   **Select a U.S. State**: state rank, volume, # change, % change, market share and top cities-MSAs  
*   **Map of Top States-Cities-MSAs**: interactive display of top cities-MSAs visited in each state  
*   **Top U.S. States Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share  
*   **Top U.S. Cities-MSAs Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share

## National Travel and Tourism Research
The National Travel and Tourism’s research products provide critical market intelligence to a range of stakeholders, including agencies within the U.S. Department of Commerce, other federal departments and agencies, Congressional offices, local and state policymakers, domestic travel and tourism industry firms and organizations, non-U.S. governments and companies, media, and academia, and more.
International Visitor Arrivals
Explore monthly and annual international visitor arrivals to the United States by their country of residence or citizenship.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
**Travel Trade Statistics**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
**Travel Trade Statistics**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.
texts.9:
# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.
texts.10:
# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Privacy
The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions.

# NTTO Updates U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.

# US National Park Travel | We recently went on a NPS/ baseball stadium trip to NY and Canada | Facebook
We recently went on a NPS/ baseball stadium trip to NY and Canada. We finished our final 6 parks in NY for a total of 376. First up was Sagamore Hill NHS, which we were surprised to find open on Labor Day. We were able to see the incredible museum, walk the grounds and on his nature trail. It was a working farm and Edith kept him humble by having him work even when President. Then off to Fire Island national seashore, where we had the undivided attention of a volunteer at the top of the lighthouse who had so much information. The volunteers even dug who knows where but found me the park brochure. At St Paul's Church NHS, the tour guide was a George Washington impersonator. Lots of interesting history and tombstones there. Next was Harriet Tubman national historic site, it was good but the site in Maryland is incredible. Fort Stanwix national monument had one of the most interesting park movies, from the perspective of the soldier. And last was Theodore Roosevelt's inaugural site NHS where we had an incredible tour guide. What was interesting at both Roosevelt sites was the videos and recordings of him. We're going to have to find an additional website as we started Canadian NPS!

# US National Park Travel | We recently went on a NPS/ baseball stadium trip to NY and Canada | Facebook
We recently went on a NPS/ baseball stadium trip to NY and Canada. We finished our final 6 parks in NY for a total of 376. First up was Sagamore Hill NHS, which we were surprised to find open on Labor Day. We were able to see the incredible museum, walk the grounds and on his nature trail. It was a working farm and Edith kept him humble by having him work even when President. Then off to Fire Island national seashore, where we had the undivided attention of a volunteer at the top of the lighthouse who had so much information. The volunteers even dug who knows where but found me the park brochure. At St Paul's Church NHS, the tour guide was a George Washington impersonator. Lots of interesting history and tombstones there. Next was Harriet Tubman national historic site, it was good but the site in Maryland is incredible. Fort Stanwix national monument had one of the most interesting park movies, from the perspective of the soldier. And last was Theodore Roosevelt's inaugural site NHS where we had an incredible tour guide. What was interesting at both Roosevelt sites was the videos and recordings of him. We're going to have to find an additional website as we started Canadian NPS!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
**Travel Trade Statistics**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. ## How much do overseas visitors spend in the USA each year?
### How much did international visitors spend in the USA in 2024?
*   International visitors spent a record **$253.9 billion** in the United States in 2024. This marked a **19% increase compared to 2023**, when spending was recorded at **$213.1 billion**3.

## What countries visit the USA the most?
*   In 2025, **Mexico** overtook **Canada** as the top source of visitor arrivals to the United States, with **17.98 million** visitors (up 6.4%) against Canada's **16.02 million** (down 20.9%)1.  
*   Excluding Canada and Mexico, the **United Kingdom**topped the list with **4.06 million** visitors, followed by **India** (2.06 million), **Japan** (1.97 million), **Brazil** (1.92 million), **Germany**(1.77 million), **South Korea** (1.65 million), **France** (1.59 million) and **China** (1.56 million)1.
Top International Tourism Source Markets for USA (2025)

## Impact of Coronavirus on Tourism
*   The pandemic caused a decline in international visitor numbers, with just **19.2 million**visitors in **2020** compared to **79.4 million** visitors in **2019**1. The following year, **2021**, saw a modest rebound, with a **16.0%** increase in visitors amounting to **22.3 million**. However, these figures still remained well below pre-pandemic levels.  
*   Tourism spending also felt the impact of the pandemic. Spending in **2020** plummeted **65%** to around **$84 billion**, down drastically from **$239 billion** in **2019**. **2021** registered a further slight decrease of **0.2%**, with total visitor spending remaining at about **$84 billion**4.

## When is the best time to visit the US?
The best time to visit the United States depends on personal preference and the specific regions of interest:
*   **Spring (March to May)**: Spring offers pleasant weather and fewer crowds compared to the summer. National parks, cities, and coastal areas are particularly enjoyable during this season.  
*   **Fall (September to November)**: Fall is a good time to explore the United States, especially for fall foliage in the Northeast and Midwest. The weather is cooler, and tourist sites are less crowded than in summer, making it an ideal time for outdoor activities.  
*   **Winter (December to February)**: Winter is the best time to visit ski resorts in the Rockies and Sierra Nevada, as well as to enjoy the warmer climates in southern states like Florida, Texas, and Arizona.  
*   **Summer (June to August)**: Summer is ideal for visiting northern regions, national parks, and coastal areas, although visitors should expect larger crowds and higher prices. This season also offers numerous outdoor festivals and events across the country.

## When is the best time to visit the US?
### When is the peak season in the US?
*   The peak travel season in the United States is generally during the summer months, from **June to August**. In 2025, **August** was the busiest month for international arrivals with **6.85 million** visitors, followed by **July** (6.25 million), while **February** was the quietest (4.65 million)2. During this period, families often take vacations, leading to increased tourism, higher prices, and larger crowds at popular destinations such as national parks, theme parks, and beaches.
Monthly International Visitor Arrivals — monthly tourism trend 2019, 2024, 2025
However, the peak season in the US also varies by region:
*   **Northeast**: The summer months mark the peak season for cities like New York City and Boston. The fall season, from September to November, also experiences increased tourism in the Northeast due to the region’s autumn foliage.  
*   **Southeast**: Beach destinations such as Florida and the Carolinas are particularly popular during the summer. The winter months, from December to February, also attract tourists to Florida as people seek to escape colder climates.  
*   **West Coast**: California experiences peak tourism in the summer, with destinations such as Los Angeles and San Francisco remaining busy year-round.  
*   **Mountain West**: Regions like the Rocky Mountains have two peak seasons: winter, for skiing and snowboarding, and summer, for hiking and outdoor activities.  
*   **Southwest**: The spring and fall months are popular in the Southwest due to milder temperatures, especially in desert regions like Arizona and Nevada.  
*   **Midwest**: Summer is the busiest season for the Midwest, with visitors travelling to cities such as Chicago and the Great Lakes region.

## Why do people travel to the United States?
In 2025, the United States welcomed tourists and visitors for a variety of reasons, as evidenced by the distribution of visa types among overseas and Mexican air and sea arrivals.
*   The majority of these arrivals, **32.05 million** (84.5%), entered on pleasure or tourism visas for activities such as vacations or visiting relatives5.  
*   Approximately **4.59 million** (12.1%) arrived on business visas.  
*   Education accounted for **1.27 million** student-visa arrivals (3.3%). Canadian visitors and Mexican land-border arrivals, a further 30.4 million, are not classified by visa type.  
*   Many people opt for road trips in the US with a total of **1.95 billion** people (both domestic and International tourists) take a road trip in 2023, where fuel cost around an $40–$70 per day.
Visitor Arrivals to the USA by Type of Visa (2025)

## What are the best places to visit in the US?
*   **National Parks:** The USA is home to some of the world’s most popular national parks, including Yellowstone National Park.  
*   **Iconic Structures:** St. Louis’s Gateway Arch National Park, which recorded 2.56 million recreation visits in 20246, represents the historical westward expansion of the United States.  
*   **Historic Sites and Monuments:** Washington, D.C., features landmarks such as the White House and the National Mall that are rich in history.  
*   **Cultural and Artistic Venues:**The USA is known for its cultural institutions, including museums with vast collections that cover global and historical artefacts, such treasures like an Egyptian temple from 10 BCE.  
*   **Natural Landscapes and Adventure:**Sedona, Arizona, also known as Red Rock Country, is popular for its natural landscape.

## What are the top visited US States?
*   In terms of the most visited US states by overseas visitors in 2025, **Florida** led as the top state with **9.3 million** visitors7, overtaking **New York** with **9.1 million** visitors. They were followed by **California** with **6.6 million** visitors, **Nevada** with **2.3 million** visitors, and **Texas** with **1.9 million** visitors.  
*   Among US cities and metropolitan areas in 2024, the New York-Newark-Jersey City region topped the list with **8.9 million** international visitors. The Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach area had **4.4 million**visitors, the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim in California welcomed **3.6 million**, Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford had **3.5 million**, and the San Francisco-Oakland-Berkeley area received **2.3 million** international visitors.  
*   In 2024, the top five states together drew **62.0%** of overseas visitors to the US, while the top five metropolitan areas accounted for **48.5%**, according to NTTO's states and cities visited monitor8.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **5. On average, per trip, Americans spend an extra $2,239.12 on traveling overseas compared to domestically**
According to Squaremouth data, from 10/1/24 to 10/1/25, U.S. travelers spent an average of $5,078.10 per domestic trip and $7,317.22 per international trip.
Due to the high cost of international trips, most travelers opt for a travel insurance plan that can fully reimburse their trip cost if they are forced to cancel.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **6. Over 85% of insurance premiums bought by U.S. travelers are for international trips**
International travel accounts for 85.97% of travel insurance premiums bought through Squaremouth.
This tells us that most Americans see international trips as higher-risk. In fact, a recent survey from Squaremouth found that 57% of travelers surveyed cited “a medical emergency abroad” as the main factor influencing their decision to buy travel insurance.
If you’re traveling overseas, it’s worth noting that standard U.S. health insurance is not widely accepted abroad. Compare travel insurance plans.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **7. Sightseeing is the number one activity Americans do when traveling abroad.**
81.5% of Americans cited “sightseeing” as their **top planned activity when traveling** abroad, regardless of whether they travel for a vacation, to visit family or friends, or for business reasons.
Unlike international tourists traveling to America#3-5, shopping was cited as the second most popular activity for Americans traveling abroad and was featured on 71.5% of Americans’ travel itineraries.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **8. 60.6% of Americans cite vacation as their primary motive for travel abroad**
Data from the International Trade Administration shows that 60.6% of Americans cite vacation as their **main reason for traveling** internationally, and 71.0% list it as a purpose of travel overall.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **9. Over 33% of Americans travel abroad for sports or outdoor activities**
In a recent survey conducted by the International Trade Administration, more than one-third of U.S. travelers said their main reason for going overseas is linked to adventure sports or physical activity.
**Popular motives include:**
*   Water sports – 12.3%  
*   Camping and hiking – 7.9%  
*   Sporting events – 7.3%  
*   Golfing and tennis – 2.3%  
*   Hunting and fishing – 2.2%  
*   Snow sports – 1.2%
This mirrors the patterns seen among international visitors coming to the U.S., with a similar share traveling for outdoor or adventure-led experiences.
Whether you’re traveling domestically within the United States or heading abroad, if your trip involves any of these activities, it’s important to check whether your travel insurance covers the specific sports you plan to take part in. Some activities may require additional protection or an upgraded policy.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **10. 2.7% of Americans travel abroad for educational purposes**
According to recent surveys conducted by the International Trade Administration, only 2.7% of U.S. travelers cite education as their primary reason for traveling overseas, a figure that closely mirrors inbound travel, where 3% of international visitors come to the U.S. for the same reason.
Across both directions, study and educational travel represent a very small share of total trips. As a result, the travel market remains overwhelmingly leisure-driven, with pricing patterns shaped far more by peak vacation seasons than by academic calendars.
Read Squaremouth’s guide to learn more about taking out travel insurance as a student when studying abroad.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **11. Business accounts for 6.5% of U.S. trips abroad**
Only 6.5% of U.S. outbound travel is for business-related purposes, notably lower than the share of international visitors coming to the U.S. for work.
This 6.5% is split between general business travel (4.5%) and attendance at conventions, conferences, and trade shows (2.0%).
Because business travel accounts for only a small proportion of outbound trips, international travel is still heavily influenced by vacation and leisure travelers.
* * *

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
Visitor behavior across the U.S. varies significantly, with major cities and world-famous attractions drawing millions each year while smaller states see far fewer international arrivals. These differences influence everything from hotel availability to regional tourism investment.
**The statistics below highlight the most-visited destinations in the country and reveal how travelers distribute themselves across states and cities.**

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **1. New York State welcomes almost 10 million international visitors**
9.8 million tourists traveled to New York State last year, more than any other state in the U.S. More specifically, the New York-White Plains-Wayne metro area, which includes New York City, attracted over 9.5 million international visitors.
New York’s popularity means hotels, attractions, and transport can be busy year-round. Booking key experiences and accommodation early is the best way to avoid premium pricing, especially in Manhattan.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **2. Neighboring New Jersey welcomes 1.23 million visitors – less than 13% of the number visiting New York State.**
Despite sitting right across the river, New Jersey attracts far fewer international tourists than New York. In 2024, New Jersey welcomed 1.23 million overseas visitors — just 12.5% of the 9.8 million who visited New York State in the same period.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **3. Florida is America’s second most-visited state**
Approximately 8.86 million international tourists visit Florida each year, with Walt Disney World being the Sunshine State’s most popular tourist destination.
The Magic Kingdom welcomes over 20 million international and domestic visitors annually, making it the ninth most-visited attraction in the U.S.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **4. Delaware is the least-visited state, with 42,000 international visitors per year**
For context, each day, Times Square gets over double the number of international visitors as Delaware does in a year’s time.
In other words, it would take Delaware 1190.47 years to welcome the same number of international visitors as Times Square has visitors per year.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **5. Times Square is the most popular tourist attraction in the U.S., with 50 million visitors every year**
That’s approximately 136,986 people every day. Meanwhile, Central Park isn’t far behind; 42 million people visit the park each year, which works out at 115,068.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **6. The Mall of America is the 4th most visited attraction in the U.S.**
With shopping being the most common activity among international visitors (81.3% of trips), it’s no surprise that the Mall of America attracts more than 40 million visitors (international and domestic) each year, making it the 4th most-visited attraction in the country.
The mall’s scale, entertainment offerings, and retail choices make it a major draw for both domestic and international travelers.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **7. San Francisco gets over 2x the number of domestic overnight visitors than it does international visitors**
In 2024, San Francisco welcomed 5.74 million domestic overnight visitors, compared with 2.34 million international visitors.
San Francisco continues to be a major destination for American travelers who account for the majority of overnight stays in the city.
For travelers, this often means considering travel insurance that covers unexpected delays or cancellations, which can be more common during high-demand periods.

## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **8. Santa Barbara is growing in popularity, with hotel occupancy up nearly 9% and airport passenger traffic rising 11% year-on-year**
Hotels in the area have recorded year-on-year occupancy increases of 8–9%, while passenger numbers through Santa Barbara Airport are up 11%.
Together, these figures point to a destination that is growing steadily in popularity, with more travelers choosing the area for its mix of coastal scenery, culture, and year-round appeal.
* * *

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **5. On average, per trip, Americans spend an extra $2,239.12 on traveling overseas compared to domestically**
According to Squaremouth data, from 10/1/24 to 10/1/25, U.S. travelers spent an average of $5,078.10 per domestic trip and $7,317.22 per international trip.
Due to the high cost of international trips, most travelers opt for a travel insurance plan that can fully reimburse their trip cost if they are forced to cancel.
texts.42:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **6. Over 85% of insurance premiums bought by U.S. travelers are for international trips**
International travel accounts for 85.97% of travel insurance premiums bought through Squaremouth.
This tells us that most Americans see international trips as higher-risk. In fact, a recent survey from Squaremouth found that 57% of travelers surveyed cited “a medical emergency abroad” as the main factor influencing their decision to buy travel insurance.
If you’re traveling overseas, it’s worth noting that standard U.S. health insurance is not widely accepted abroad. Compare travel insurance plans.
texts.43:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **7. Sightseeing is the number one activity Americans do when traveling abroad.**
81.5% of Americans cited “sightseeing” as their **top planned activity when traveling** abroad, regardless of whether they travel for a vacation, to visit family or friends, or for business reasons.
Unlike international tourists traveling to America#3-5, shopping was cited as the second most popular activity for Americans traveling abroad and was featured on 71.5% of Americans’ travel itineraries.
texts.44:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **8. 60.6% of Americans cite vacation as their primary motive for travel abroad**
Data from the International Trade Administration shows that 60.6% of Americans cite vacation as their **main reason for traveling** internationally, and 71.0% list it as a purpose of travel overall.
texts.45:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **9. Over 33% of Americans travel abroad for sports or outdoor activities**
In a recent survey conducted by the International Trade Administration, more than one-third of U.S. travelers said their main reason for going overseas is linked to adventure sports or physical activity.
**Popular motives include:**
*   Water sports – 12.3%  
*   Camping and hiking – 7.9%  
*   Sporting events – 7.3%  
*   Golfing and tennis – 2.3%  
*   Hunting and fishing – 2.2%  
*   Snow sports – 1.2%
This mirrors the patterns seen among international visitors coming to the U.S., with a similar share traveling for outdoor or adventure-led experiences.
Whether you’re traveling domestically within the United States or heading abroad, if your trip involves any of these activities, it’s important to check whether your travel insurance covers the specific sports you plan to take part in. Some activities may require additional protection or an upgraded policy.
texts.46:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **10. 2.7% of Americans travel abroad for educational purposes**
According to recent surveys conducted by the International Trade Administration, only 2.7% of U.S. travelers cite education as their primary reason for traveling overseas, a figure that closely mirrors inbound travel, where 3% of international visitors come to the U.S. for the same reason.
Across both directions, study and educational travel represent a very small share of total trips. As a result, the travel market remains overwhelmingly leisure-driven, with pricing patterns shaped far more by peak vacation seasons than by academic calendars.
Read Squaremouth’s guide to learn more about taking out travel insurance as a student when studying abroad.
texts.47:
## Americans Abroad: Outbound U.S. Travel & Tourism Statistics
### **11. Business accounts for 6.5% of U.S. trips abroad**
Only 6.5% of U.S. outbound travel is for business-related purposes, notably lower than the share of international visitors coming to the U.S. for work.
This 6.5% is split between general business travel (4.5%) and attendance at conventions, conferences, and trade shows (2.0%).
Because business travel accounts for only a small proportion of outbound trips, international travel is still heavily influenced by vacation and leisure travelers.
* * *
texts.48:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
Visitor behavior across the U.S. varies significantly, with major cities and world-famous attractions drawing millions each year while smaller states see far fewer international arrivals. These differences influence everything from hotel availability to regional tourism investment.
**The statistics below highlight the most-visited destinations in the country and reveal how travelers distribute themselves across states and cities.**
texts.49:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **1. New York State welcomes almost 10 million international visitors**
9.8 million tourists traveled to New York State last year, more than any other state in the U.S. More specifically, the New York-White Plains-Wayne metro area, which includes New York City, attracted over 9.5 million international visitors.
New York’s popularity means hotels, attractions, and transport can be busy year-round. Booking key experiences and accommodation early is the best way to avoid premium pricing, especially in Manhattan.
texts.50:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **2. Neighboring New Jersey welcomes 1.23 million visitors – less than 13% of the number visiting New York State.**
Despite sitting right across the river, New Jersey attracts far fewer international tourists than New York. In 2024, New Jersey welcomed 1.23 million overseas visitors — just 12.5% of the 9.8 million who visited New York State in the same period.
texts.51:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **3. Florida is America’s second most-visited state**
Approximately 8.86 million international tourists visit Florida each year, with Walt Disney World being the Sunshine State’s most popular tourist destination.
The Magic Kingdom welcomes over 20 million international and domestic visitors annually, making it the ninth most-visited attraction in the U.S.
texts.52:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **4. Delaware is the least-visited state, with 42,000 international visitors per year**
For context, each day, Times Square gets over double the number of international visitors as Delaware does in a year’s time.
In other words, it would take Delaware 1190.47 years to welcome the same number of international visitors as Times Square has visitors per year.
texts.53:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **5. Times Square is the most popular tourist attraction in the U.S., with 50 million visitors every year**
That’s approximately 136,986 people every day. Meanwhile, Central Park isn’t far behind; 42 million people visit the park each year, which works out at 115,068.
texts.54:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **6. The Mall of America is the 4th most visited attraction in the U.S.**
With shopping being the most common activity among international visitors (81.3% of trips), it’s no surprise that the Mall of America attracts more than 40 million visitors (international and domestic) each year, making it the 4th most-visited attraction in the country.
The mall’s scale, entertainment offerings, and retail choices make it a major draw for both domestic and international travelers.
texts.55:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **7. San Francisco gets over 2x the number of domestic overnight visitors than it does international visitors**
In 2024, San Francisco welcomed 5.74 million domestic overnight visitors, compared with 2.34 million international visitors.
San Francisco continues to be a major destination for American travelers who account for the majority of overnight stays in the city.
For travelers, this often means considering travel insurance that covers unexpected delays or cancellations, which can be more common during high-demand periods.
texts.56:
## U.S. Tourism Statistics by State & City
### **8. Santa Barbara is growing in popularity, with hotel occupancy up nearly 9% and airport passenger traffic rising 11% year-on-year**
Hotels in the area have recorded year-on-year occupancy increases of 8–9%, while passenger numbers through Santa Barbara Airport are up 11%.
Together, these figures point to a destination that is growing steadily in popularity, with more travelers choosing the area for its mix of coastal scenery, culture, and year-round appeal.
* * *

## How much do overseas visitors spend in the USA each year?
### How much did international visitors spend in the USA in 2024?
*   International visitors spent a record **$253.9 billion** in the United States in 2024. This marked a **19% increase compared to 2023**, when spending was recorded at **$213.1 billion**3.
texts.8:
## What countries visit the USA the most?
*   In 2025, **Mexico** overtook **Canada** as the top source of visitor arrivals to the United States, with **17.98 million** visitors (up 6.4%) against Canada's **16.02 million** (down 20.9%)1.  
*   Excluding Canada and Mexico, the **United Kingdom**topped the list with **4.06 million** visitors, followed by **India** (2.06 million), **Japan** (1.97 million), **Brazil** (1.92 million), **Germany**(1.77 million), **South Korea** (1.65 million), **France** (1.59 million) and **China** (1.56 million)1.

texts.9:
## Impact of Coronavirus on Tourism
*   The pandemic caused a decline in international visitor numbers, with just **19.2 million**visitors in **2020** compared to **79.4 million** visitors in **2019**1. The following year, **2021**, saw a modest rebound, with a **16.0%** increase in visitors amounting to **22.3 million**. However, these figures still remained well below pre-pandemic levels.  
*   Tourism spending also felt the impact of the pandemic. Spending in **2020** plummeted **65%** to around **$84 billion**, down drastically from **$239 billion** in **2019**. **2021** registered a further slight decrease of **0.2%**, with total visitor spending remaining at about **$84 billion**4.
texts.10:
## When is the best time to visit the US?
The best time to visit the United States depends on personal preference and the specific regions of interest:
*   **Spring (March to May)**: Spring offers pleasant weather and fewer crowds compared to the summer. National parks, cities, and coastal areas are particularly enjoyable during this season.  
*   **Fall (September to November)**: Fall is a good time to explore the United States, especially for fall foliage in the Northeast and Midwest. The weather is cooler, and tourist sites are less crowded than in summer, making it an ideal time for outdoor activities.  
*   **Winter (December to February)**: Winter is the best time to visit ski resorts in the Rockies and Sierra Nevada, as well as to enjoy the warmer climates in southern states like Florida, Texas, and Arizona.  
*   **Summer (June to August)**: Summer is ideal for visiting northern regions, national parks, and coastal areas, although visitors should expect larger crowds and higher prices. This season also offers numerous outdoor festivals and events across the country.
texts.11:
## When is the best time to visit the US?
### When is the peak season in the US?
*   The peak travel season in the United States is generally during the summer months, from **June to August**. In 2025, **August** was the busiest month for international arrivals with **6.85 million** visitors, followed by **July** (6.25 million), while **February** was the quietest (4.65 million)2. During this period, families often take vacations, leading to increased tourism, higher prices, and larger crowds at popular destinations such as national parks, theme parks, and beaches.
Monthly International Visitor Arrivals — monthly tourism trend 2019, 2024, 2025
However, the peak season in the US also varies by region:
*   **Northeast**: The summer months mark the peak season for cities like New York City and Boston. The fall season, from September to November, also experiences increased tourism in the Northeast due to the region’s autumn foliage.  
*   **Southeast**: Beach destinations such as Florida and the Carolinas are particularly popular during the summer. The winter months, from December to February, also attract tourists to Florida as people seek to escape colder climates.  
*   **West Coast**: California experiences peak tourism in the summer, with destinations such as Los Angeles and San Francisco remaining busy year-round.  
*   **Mountain West**: Regions like the Rocky Mountains have two peak seasons: winter, for skiing and snowboarding, and summer, for hiking and outdoor activities.  
*   **Southwest**: The spring and fall months are popular in the Southwest due to milder temperatures, especially in desert regions like Arizona and Nevada.  
*   **Midwest**: Summer is the busiest season for the Midwest, with visitors travelling to cities such as Chicago and the Great Lakes region.
texts.12:
## Why do people travel to the United States?
In 2025, the United States welcomed tourists and visitors for a variety of reasons, as evidenced by the distribution of visa types among overseas and Mexican air and sea arrivals.
*   The majority of these arrivals, **32.05 million** (84.5%), entered on pleasure or tourism visas for activities such as vacations or visiting relatives5.  
*   Approximately **4.59 million** (12.1%) arrived on business visas.  
*   Education accounted for **1.27 million** student-visa arrivals (3.3%). Canadian visitors and Mexican land-border arrivals, a further 30.4 million, are not classified by visa type.  
*   Many people opt for road trips in the US with a total of **1.95 billion** people (both domestic and International tourists) take a road trip in 2023, where fuel cost around an $40–$70 per day.

An Air IndiaBoeing 747-400 arrives at John F. Kennedy International Airport, with El Al Israel and Swiss International jets at Terminal 4 in 2004. JFK is the largest entry point for international arrivals to the United States.
The New York metropolitan area has the busiest airport system in the United States and the second-busiest in the world after London. It is the country's most frequently used port of entry and departure for international flights.
The metro area has three major airports: John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), LaGuardia Airport (LGA), and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), all operated since 1947 by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-1) In 2024, they were used by more than 146.1 million passengers.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-2) With 142.7 million passengers, 2025 was the third busiest year, just behind 2023 (143.8 million passengers).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-3) Until October 2022, the three shared the International Air Transport Association airport code (IATA code) "NYC"; Newark only uses EWR as of the change.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-5) JFK and Newark are connected to regional rail systems by AirTrain JFK and AirTrain Newark respectively.
The class B airspace used by the three airports is extremely congested. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) limits the number of flights per hour but they rank among the top five airports in the United States for delays.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-7)

The area also includes several satellite or reliever airports that provide commercial air carrier service on a much smaller scale as well as numerous general aviation airports, heliports, and seaplane bases.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-8)

Teterboro Airport is the oldest operating airport in the New York metropolitan area. Walter C. Teter (1863–1929) acquired the property in 1917.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-9) While other localities had municipal airports, New York City itself had a multitude of private airfields, and thus did not see the need for a municipal airport until the late 1920s.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-11)Flushing Airport opened in 1927, quickly becoming the city's busiest airport; it closed in 1984.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-:0-12)Newark Liberty International Airport opened in 1928.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-13) It was followed in 1930 by Floyd Bennett Field: New York City's first municipal airport, built largely to serve the growth of commercial aviation after World War I.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-14)LaGuardia Airport was opened in 1939,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-15) and Floyd Bennett Field was closed for general aviation two years later.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-:1-16)John F. Kennedy International Airport opened as Idlewild Airport in 1948.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-17)

From the 1940s through the 1970s, many airlines provided ticketing, baggage, and airport ground transportation services at remote terminals located in Manhattan. The need for remote terminals arose because at that time airlines were competing with traditional forms of transportation (e.g., railroads) that operated between city centers and there were limitations in passenger processing capacity and parking supply at airports.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Gosling-18) The 42nd Street Airlines Terminal opened in 1941 on Park Avenue across from Grand Central Terminal. Traffic congestion on streets in the area of the 42nd Street Airlines Terminal led to the opening of the East Side Airlines Terminal in 1953 to provide service to Idlewild and La Guardia airports from its location near the entrance to the Queens–Midtown Tunnel and the opening of the West Side Airlines Terminal in 1955 to provide service to Newark Airport from its location near the entrance to the Lincoln Tunnel. After the opening of these new remote terminals the 42nd Street Airlines Terminal was renamed the Airlines Building and became a ticketing-only facility.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Deco-19) By the early 1970s, there was less need for remote terminals because most airlines had acquired better ticketing and baggage handling facilities at the airports and more air passengers were traveling to or from the suburbs rather than having trip origins or destinations in Manhattan.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Gosling-18) The West Side Airlines Terminal closed in 1972, the Airlines Building was demolished in 1978, and the East Side Airlines Terminal closed in 1984.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Deco-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-20)
The Aviation Hall of Fame and Museum of New Jersey, Cradle of Aviation Museum, Marine Air Terminal and Newark Metropolitan Airport Buildings preserve the history of aviation in the New York metro area.

*   September 11 attacks

The vast majority of airspace above the metropolitan area is controlled by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and split into complex sectors that organize the flow of flights to and from the area's many airports, as well as transitory air traffic between neighboring regions.
*   New York Air Route Traffic Control Center (ZNY) in Ronkonkoma, Long Island, is one of 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers (ARTCC) in the United States. It is responsible for high-altitude traffic above the New York Metropolitan Area and Philadelphia/Delaware Valley metro area, as well as 3,250,000 square miles (8,400,000 km 2) of oceanic airspace.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-21) The unit was located at JFK Airport until July 1963, when it moved to a purpose-built site in Suffolk County that was designed to resist a nuclear attack.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-22)  
*   New York TRACON (N90), located in Westbury, Long Island, is one of seven large terminal radar approach control units in the United States. It handles air traffic in southern New York State and southeastern Connecticut.  
*   Philadelphia TRACON as of July 2024 handles air traffic for Northern New Jersey airports.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-23)
