## Key Highlights
*   New York City has three main airports. These are John F. Kennedy (JFK), LaGuardia (LGA), and Newark Liberty (EWR).  
*   JFK is the main international airport in the city. Most international flights and those that go a long way start or end here.  
*   LaGuardia Airport mostly deals with domestic flights inside the United States.  
*   Newark Liberty International Airport is in New Jersey. People use it for both international flights and domestic trips.  
*   Smaller airports like Stewart (SWF) and MacArthur (ISP) are also here. They give you more ways to fly into the New York area.  
*   There is a lot of construction right now at JFK. This might make it take longer for you to get to or from the airport.

## Introduction
Welcome to your easy guide for getting around airports in New York City! Your trip to New York starts as soon as you land. Picking the right airport can really help you have a better time while you travel. There are a few big airports in the New York metropolitan area. It is not always easy to choose which airport is good for you. This guide will show you all you need to know about each airport. You will find info about where they are, how to get to the city, which airlines use them, and what you can find there.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
The New York City metropolitan area is a busy place for travelers. The area has many airports that are run by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, along with other groups. Most people know about the main three airports, but there are also smaller airports in New York State and New Jersey that can be easy for people to use.
It is important to know how each airport is different. This can help you when you plan your trip. Below, you can see information about the biggest international airports and some smaller regional or private ones that you may want to use.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 1. John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)
John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) is about 16 miles from Manhattan. It is in the borough of Queens and is one of the main international airports in the United States. Most people use JFK airport as the city’s main gateway for international flights. There are usually a lot of people there, so it can get busy and crowded. The lines at customs and baggage claim can be long. Sometimes you will need an hour, and sometimes up to two hours, depending on how many flights get in around the same time.
Kennedy International Airport is an important place for airlines such as American Airlines and Delta Air Lines. Many people from around the world travel in and out of this airport. If you want to fly in from another country, this is a good airport to use. There is a big redevelopment happening at JFK now, so it is smart to give yourself extra time, as you could run into delays from construction.
This international airport is managed by the Port Authority. You will find the AirTrain there. The AirTrain connects to the New York subway, so it is a cheap way for people to get to Manhattan from JFK airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 2. LaGuardia Airport (LGA)
LaGuardia Airport (LGA) is in Queens, New York. It is the nearest major airport to Manhattan. It is about eight miles away from the city. Most flights at LaGuardia are domestic flights, so you will not fly here from outside North America. You will use LaGuardia if you are connecting to another U.S. city or coming in from another part of the country.
In the last few years, LaGuardia Airport has changed a lot. Terminal B is now new, and Terminal C got a big update. Delta Air Lines mainly uses Terminal C now. The new look and better spaces make the airport easier to use and much more comfortable.
Getting to Manhattan is easy because the airport is so close. Buses are the main way to use public transit, but not everyone likes this option. Taxis and rideshare services are popular and can be quick, but it depends on traffic. The Port Authority of New York runs LaGuardia Airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 3. Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR)
Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) is in Newark, New Jersey. It sits about 17 miles from Manhattan. Even though it’s in a different state, the airport is one of the main three that serve the New York City area. At Newark Liberty International Airport, you can find a busy list of both domestic and international flights. This makes it a good airport for many people flying in and out of New York City.
This is a major spot for United Airlines. From here, there is a big web of flights to all parts of the world. American Airlines and some other airlines also fly here. While Newark Liberty International is smaller than JFK, you should still plan for about one to two hours to get through customs and baggage claim.
Since the airport is in New Jersey, getting to Manhattan can cost a bit more. But travelers have the AirTrain Newark, which goes right to NJ Transit trains. This is an easy and direct way to get to Penn Station in Midtown Manhattan from Newark Liberty International Airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 4. New York Stewart International Airport (SWF)
New York Stewart International Airport (SWF) is an airport that serves the New York metropolitan area, but it is much farther away from Manhattan. It sits about 65 miles north of Manhattan in New York State. This airport is less busy than the main ones around the city. At Stewart International Airport, you will find both domestic flights and a few international ones.
The airlines that fly to and from SWF may change from time to time. In the past, some low-cost airlines have used it for trips across the Atlantic Ocean. If you want to fly from Stewart International Airport, it’s smart to check which airlines are flying out of there right now.
Because this airport is far from Manhattan, getting into the city can cost more and take longer than other airports. You can get there by airport bus, private cars, or by taking local trains and buses together. The Federal Aviation Administration manages the air traffic for SWF, so it is safe and works well as an entry point in the region, even if it is not close to the city.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 5. Westchester County Airport (HPN)
Westchester County Airport (HPN) is in White Plains, New York. It is about 30 miles north of Manhattan. This airport is smaller and easier to use for domestic flights. You do not get the big crowds that are in other airports here. The lines are not as long and you can get around the place faster.
If you want to go to Westchester County, Connecticut, or the north part of the metropolitan area, this airport is a good choice. It can make your trip simpler and save you time.
At Westchester County Airport, most flights stay inside the United States. You can fly with American Airlines or Delta Air Lines. The airport has flights to big cities like Chicago, Atlanta, and places in Florida. So, you do not need to deal with the busy and crowded airports in New York City.
The Port Authority does not run this airport. But it still has an important part in the New York State air travel system. You have a few ways to get to or from Manhattan. There are taxis and car services. You can also go to a station nearby and take the Metro-North Railroad to the city.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 6. Long Island MacArthur Airport (ISP)
Long Island MacArthur Airport (ISP) is in Ronkonkoma on Long Island. It’s a good airport for the greater New York State area. This airport is around 50 miles east of Manhattan. Many people on Long Island pick this airport, and it’s also good for anyone who wants to stay away from the busy crowds at JFK and LaGuardia. People like this airport because getting in and out is easy, and being there is not stressful.
MacArthur Airport handles domestic flights. You will find airlines like Southwest Airlines here, and they fly to lots of places in the country. Frontier Airlines and a few more low-cost carriers also use this airport. These options help travelers save money on flights.
Getting from Long Island MacArthur Airport to New York City is also simple. The airport sits close to Ronkonkoma station on the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR). The LIRR gives you a direct ride to Penn Station in Manhattan. This makes it easy for travelers going to New York City to get there.

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Terminal Layout and Facilities
The user experience at New York airports is getting better fast. LaGuardia, which some people used to say was old, now has a brand new Terminal B and a modern Terminal C. These new airport terminals are big and bright. They have art for people to enjoy and many updated shops and restaurants.
Newark also got a new Terminal A. This new terminal has lots of updated features. People move in and out more easily, and there are local places to eat.
JFK is working on a new airport plan. It’s making all the old terminals into one group of world-class new airport terminals. This work will give people a better passenger terminal when it’s finished.
There is some construction at JFK now, and it may be a problem for some. But when it’s all done, the whole airport will be much better. All three airports want to give people more things they need—from better security, to comfy gate areas, and better places to relax in the lounge.

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Pros and Cons of Each Airport
Picking the best airport for your trip means you have to think about what matters most to you. Some people go for the lowest price, some want easy travel, and others may need more flight options. The right airport for you will depend on what you look for first.
*   **JFK International Airport:**  
    *   **Pros:** It’s one of the best airports in the area if you need international flights. This international airport gives you the most airlines to pick from. The AirTrain makes it easy to get there by public transit.  
    *   **Cons:** It can get very busy. Because of the crowds, you may spend more time at the security checkpoint and at customs. There is often building or road work, which can lead to delays.

*   **LaGuardia Airport (LGA):**  
    *   **Pros:** This airport is the closest one to Manhattan. That gives you cheaper taxi rides. If you want domestic flights, you may like the new, modern terminals here.  
    *   **Cons:** There is not a good way to get to this airport by public transit. There can be flight delays because many planes use LaGuardia Airport at the same time.

*   **Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR):**  
    *   **Pros:** This is another international airport. It’s usually not as crowded as JFK. Newark Liberty International has a good train that takes you right to Manhattan. If you like United Airlines, you will find many flights here.  
    *   **Cons

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Best Airport for International Flights
When people travel overseas from New York, the best airport to choose is John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). It is the main international airport in New York. JFK offers more overseas flights than any other airport in the area. If you want nonstop flights from Europe, Asia, South America, or many other places, JFK will be your best pick most of the time.
Kennedy International Airport has many top airlines. You will see carriers such as British Airways, Air France, Singapore Airlines, and Air India with flights every day. This big group of airlines lets you have more choices to travel nonstop to big cities around the world.
Even though Newark (EWR) also has many international flights, and it works closely with United Airlines, most people pick Kennedy International Airport. This is because there are more airlines and flights here. The airport also has large spaces to help big groups of people who are flying overseas. It has good customs and immigration services too.

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Best Airport for Domestic Flights
If you are planning to travel in the United States, LaGuardia Airport (LGA) is often the best choice. The main reason is that it is close to Manhattan. This means you spend less time on the road and pay less for taxis or ride shares. So, if you have a quick business trip or want a weekend away from another city in the United States, LGA is hard to beat.
LaGuardia Airport is home to big airlines like American Airlines and Delta. They have many flights that go to different places across the country. The Port Authority of New York spent a lot of money to upgrade this airport. Now, it is modern, comfortable, and easy to use.
Other airports in New York, like JFK and Newark, also have many domestic flights. Southwest Airlines also flies from LGA. But because LaGuardia Airport mainly does domestic flights and it is so close to the city, it really is the best option if you want something easy and fast. Just remember, traffic can get busy, so it is smart to check how the drive looks, especially when lots of people are on the road.

## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
After you land, you need to get into Manhattan. The good news is that New York has many ways to travel, so you can find what works best for you. There are cheap options like the subway and bus services. There are also airport shuttles that are easy to use. If you want a quick and easy ride, you can pick a taxi or use a rideshare.
No matter if you want to save money and use public transport, want the easy pick of an airport shuttle, or just want the comfort of a private car, you will find something that works. You can get from your gate to your hotel near Grand Central or any other place you want to go. Now, let’s see some good ways to finish your trip in New York.

## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
### Airport Shuttle Services
Airport shuttle services give you a nice way to travel that sits between using public transit and taking a private car. These are vans or buses that you share with other people. This way is easy for you and does not cost much. It gets you from the airport to your hotel or other place in the city. You will usually see these shuttles waiting in special spots outside the baggage claim area.
There are a few companies that run shared shuttle services at JFK, LaGuardia, and Newark. You will be with other people in the shuttle, so there may be many stops. But it is nice that you get dropped off right at your hotel. The Port Authority website can help you by listing which bus services and shuttle companies are allowed to pick you up at each airport.
Here are some key points about airport shuttles:
*   They are not as expensive as a taxi or a private car.  
*   You can often get your spot ahead of time by booking online.  
*   How long the ride takes can change depending on traffic or how many stops there are.  
*   Make sure you use official bus services and go to the main shuttle counters in the airport so you do not get caught in a scam.

## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
### Public Transit (Subway, Train, Bus)
Taking public transit is the best way to save money when you travel from New York’s airports to New York City. All three main airports are linked to the city by public transit, but each one is a bit different. This way of getting around works well if you do not have much luggage, and you get to see New York City like people who live here.
If you arrive at JFK, you can ride the AirTrain, and then switch to the subway or Long Island Rail Road (LIRR). For Newark, use the AirTrain, which connects to NJ Transit trains going right to Penn Station. From LaGuardia, you can use city bus services. These will take you to different subway lines that go all over the metropolitan area.
Here is how to use public transit:
*   **JFK:** AirTrain and then take the Subway (A, E, J, Z lines) or switch to LIRR.  
*   **EWR:** AirTrain then use the NJ Transit train straight to Penn Station.  
*   **LGA:** Q70-SBS LaGuardia Link bus, which is free, to subway lines 7, E, F, M, R.  
*   This is the cheapest way, but you may have to change trains or buses and carry your bags up and down stairs.

What is an IATA three-letter airport code?
United States airports, as well as airports around the world use a universal unique three-letter airport code, or Location Identifier defined by the International Air Transport Association. It's easier to say, and write LAX than Los Angeles International Airport for the pilots, controllers, travel agents, frequent flyers, computers and baggage handlers. It's the three-letter code you see on baggage tags in the airport.
Are there four-character codes?
The ICAO airport code is a four-character alphanumeric code used to designate all airport around the world as defined by the International Civil Aviation Organization. ICAO codes differ from the IATA codes used for reservations and baggage, as they are used by air traffic control for flight planning and airline operations, and are not included in this list.

An Air IndiaBoeing 747-400 arrives at John F. Kennedy International Airport, with El Al Israel and Swiss International jets at Terminal 4 in 2004. JFK is the largest entry point for international arrivals to the United States.
The New York metropolitan area has the busiest airport system in the United States and the second-busiest in the world after London. It is the country's most frequently used port of entry and departure for international flights.
The metro area has three major airports: John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), LaGuardia Airport (LGA), and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), all operated since 1947 by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-1) In 2024, they were used by more than 146.1 million passengers.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-2) With 142.7 million passengers, 2025 was the third busiest year, just behind 2023 (143.8 million passengers).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-3) Until October 2022, the three shared the International Air Transport Association airport code (IATA code) "NYC"; Newark only uses EWR as of the change.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-5) JFK and Newark are connected to regional rail systems by AirTrain JFK and AirTrain Newark respectively.
The class B airspace used by the three airports is extremely congested. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) limits the number of flights per hour but they rank among the top five airports in the United States for delays.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-7)

From the 1940s through the 1970s, many airlines provided ticketing, baggage, and airport ground transportation services at remote terminals located in Manhattan. The need for remote terminals arose because at that time airlines were competing with traditional forms of transportation (e.g., railroads) that operated between city centers and there were limitations in passenger processing capacity and parking supply at airports.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Gosling-18) The 42nd Street Airlines Terminal opened in 1941 on Park Avenue across from Grand Central Terminal. Traffic congestion on streets in the area of the 42nd Street Airlines Terminal led to the opening of the East Side Airlines Terminal in 1953 to provide service to Idlewild and La Guardia airports from its location near the entrance to the Queens–Midtown Tunnel and the opening of the West Side Airlines Terminal in 1955 to provide service to Newark Airport from its location near the entrance to the Lincoln Tunnel. After the opening of these new remote terminals the 42nd Street Airlines Terminal was renamed the Airlines Building and became a ticketing-only facility.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Deco-19) By the early 1970s, there was less need for remote terminals because most airlines had acquired better ticketing and baggage handling facilities at the airports and more air passengers were traveling to or from the suburbs rather than having trip origins or destinations in Manhattan.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Gosling-18) The West Side Airlines Terminal closed in 1972, the Airlines Building was demolished in 1978, and the East Side Airlines Terminal closed in 1984.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-Deco-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area#cite_note-20)
The Aviation Hall of Fame and Museum of New Jersey, Cradle of Aviation Museum, Marine Air Terminal and Newark Metropolitan Airport Buildings preserve the history of aviation in the New York metro area.

What is an IATA three-letter airport code?
United States airports, as well as airports around the world use a universal unique three-letter airport code, or Location Identifier defined by the International Air Transport Association. It's easier to say, and write LAX than Los Angeles International Airport for the pilots, controllers, travel agents, frequent flyers, computers and baggage handlers. It's the three-letter code you see on baggage tags in the airport.
Are there four-character codes?
The ICAO airport code is a four-character alphanumeric code used to designate all airport around the world as defined by the International Civil Aviation Organization. ICAO codes differ from the IATA codes used for reservations and baggage, as they are used by air traffic control for flight planning and airline operations, and are not included in this list.

## Key Highlights
*   New York City has three main airports. These are John F. Kennedy (JFK), LaGuardia (LGA), and Newark Liberty (EWR).  
*   JFK is the main international airport in the city. Most international flights and those that go a long way start or end here.  
*   LaGuardia Airport mostly deals with domestic flights inside the United States.  
*   Newark Liberty International Airport is in New Jersey. People use it for both international flights and domestic trips.  
*   Smaller airports like Stewart (SWF) and MacArthur (ISP) are also here. They give you more ways to fly into the New York area.  
*   There is a lot of construction right now at JFK. This might make it take longer for you to get to or from the airport.

## Introduction
Welcome to your easy guide for getting around airports in New York City! Your trip to New York starts as soon as you land. Picking the right airport can really help you have a better time while you travel. There are a few big airports in the New York metropolitan area. It is not always easy to choose which airport is good for you. This guide will show you all you need to know about each airport. You will find info about where they are, how to get to the city, which airlines use them, and what you can find there.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
The New York City metropolitan area is a busy place for travelers. The area has many airports that are run by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, along with other groups. Most people know about the main three airports, but there are also smaller airports in New York State and New Jersey that can be easy for people to use.
It is important to know how each airport is different. This can help you when you plan your trip. Below, you can see information about the biggest international airports and some smaller regional or private ones that you may want to use.
texts.3:
## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 1. John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)
John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) is about 16 miles from Manhattan. It is in the borough of Queens and is one of the main international airports in the United States. Most people use JFK airport as the city’s main gateway for international flights. There are usually a lot of people there, so it can get busy and crowded. The lines at customs and baggage claim can be long. Sometimes you will need an hour, and sometimes up to two hours, depending on how many flights get in around the same time.
Kennedy International Airport is an important place for airlines such as American Airlines and Delta Air Lines. Many people from around the world travel in and out of this airport. If you want to fly in from another country, this is a good airport to use. There is a big redevelopment happening at JFK now, so it is smart to give yourself extra time, as you could run into delays from construction.
This international airport is managed by the Port Authority. You will find the AirTrain there. The AirTrain connects to the New York subway, so it is a cheap way for people to get to Manhattan from JFK airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 2. LaGuardia Airport (LGA)
LaGuardia Airport (LGA) is in Queens, New York. It is the nearest major airport to Manhattan. It is about eight miles away from the city. Most flights at LaGuardia are domestic flights, so you will not fly here from outside North America. You will use LaGuardia if you are connecting to another U.S. city or coming in from another part of the country.
In the last few years, LaGuardia Airport has changed a lot. Terminal B is now new, and Terminal C got a big update. Delta Air Lines mainly uses Terminal C now. The new look and better spaces make the airport easier to use and much more comfortable.
Getting to Manhattan is easy because the airport is so close. Buses are the main way to use public transit, but not everyone likes this option. Taxis and rideshare services are popular and can be quick, but it depends on traffic. The Port Authority of New York runs LaGuardia Airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 3. Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR)
Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) is in Newark, New Jersey. It sits about 17 miles from Manhattan. Even though it’s in a different state, the airport is one of the main three that serve the New York City area. At Newark Liberty International Airport, you can find a busy list of both domestic and international flights. This makes it a good airport for many people flying in and out of New York City.
This is a major spot for United Airlines. From here, there is a big web of flights to all parts of the world. American Airlines and some other airlines also fly here. While Newark Liberty International is smaller than JFK, you should still plan for about one to two hours to get through customs and baggage claim.
Since the airport is in New Jersey, getting to Manhattan can cost a bit more. But travelers have the AirTrain Newark, which goes right to NJ Transit trains. This is an easy and direct way to get to Penn Station in Midtown Manhattan from Newark Liberty International Airport.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 4. New York Stewart International Airport (SWF)
New York Stewart International Airport (SWF) is an airport that serves the New York metropolitan area, but it is much farther away from Manhattan. It sits about 65 miles north of Manhattan in New York State. This airport is less busy than the main ones around the city. At Stewart International Airport, you will find both domestic flights and a few international ones.
The airlines that fly to and from SWF may change from time to time. In the past, some low-cost airlines have used it for trips across the Atlantic Ocean. If you want to fly from Stewart International Airport, it’s smart to check which airlines are flying out of there right now.
Because this airport is far from Manhattan, getting into the city can cost more and take longer than other airports. You can get there by airport bus, private cars, or by taking local trains and buses together. The Federal Aviation Administration manages the air traffic for SWF, so it is safe and works well as an entry point in the region, even if it is not close to the city.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 5. Westchester County Airport (HPN)
Westchester County Airport (HPN) is in White Plains, New York. It is about 30 miles north of Manhattan. This airport is smaller and easier to use for domestic flights. You do not get the big crowds that are in other airports here. The lines are not as long and you can get around the place faster.
If you want to go to Westchester County, Connecticut, or the north part of the metropolitan area, this airport is a good choice. It can make your trip simpler and save you time.
At Westchester County Airport, most flights stay inside the United States. You can fly with American Airlines or Delta Air Lines. The airport has flights to big cities like Chicago, Atlanta, and places in Florida. So, you do not need to deal with the busy and crowded airports in New York City.
The Port Authority does not run this airport. But it still has an important part in the New York State air travel system. You have a few ways to get to or from Manhattan. There are taxis and car services. You can also go to a station nearby and take the Metro-North Railroad to the city.

## Comprehensive List of New York Airports for Travelers
### 6. Long Island MacArthur Airport (ISP)
Long Island MacArthur Airport (ISP) is in Ronkonkoma on Long Island. It’s a good airport for the greater New York State area. This airport is around 50 miles east of Manhattan. Many people on Long Island pick this airport, and it’s also good for anyone who wants to stay away from the busy crowds at JFK and LaGuardia. People like this airport because getting in and out is easy, and being there is not stressful.
MacArthur Airport handles domestic flights. You will find airlines like Southwest Airlines here, and they fly to lots of places in the country. Frontier Airlines and a few more low-cost carriers also use this airport. These options help travelers save money on flights.
Getting from Long Island MacArthur Airport to New York City is also simple. The airport sits close to Ronkonkoma station on the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR). The LIRR gives you a direct ride to Penn Station in Manhattan. This makes it easy for travelers going to New York City to get there.

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Terminal Layout and Facilities
The user experience at New York airports is getting better fast. LaGuardia, which some people used to say was old, now has a brand new Terminal B and a modern Terminal C. These new airport terminals are big and bright. They have art for people to enjoy and many updated shops and restaurants.
Newark also got a new Terminal A. This new terminal has lots of updated features. People move in and out more easily, and there are local places to eat.
JFK is working on a new airport plan. It’s making all the old terminals into one group of world-class new airport terminals. This work will give people a better passenger terminal when it’s finished.
There is some construction at JFK now, and it may be a problem for some. But when it’s all done, the whole airport will be much better. All three airports want to give people more things they need—from better security, to comfy gate areas, and better places to relax in the lounge.

## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Best Airport for International Flights
When people travel overseas from New York, the best airport to choose is John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). It is the main international airport in New York. JFK offers more overseas flights than any other airport in the area. If you want nonstop flights from Europe, Asia, South America, or many other places, JFK will be your best pick most of the time.
Kennedy International Airport has many top airlines. You will see carriers such as British Airways, Air France, Singapore Airlines, and Air India with flights every day. This big group of airlines lets you have more choices to travel nonstop to big cities around the world.
Even though Newark (EWR) also has many international flights, and it works closely with United Airlines, most people pick Kennedy International Airport. This is because there are more airlines and flights here. The airport also has large spaces to help big groups of people who are flying overseas. It has good customs and immigration services too.
texts.17:
## Comparing New York’s Major Airports: JFK, LGA, and EWR
### Best Airport for Domestic Flights
If you are planning to travel in the United States, LaGuardia Airport (LGA) is often the best choice. The main reason is that it is close to Manhattan. This means you spend less time on the road and pay less for taxis or ride shares. So, if you have a quick business trip or want a weekend away from another city in the United States, LGA is hard to beat.
LaGuardia Airport is home to big airlines like American Airlines and Delta. They have many flights that go to different places across the country. The Port Authority of New York spent a lot of money to upgrade this airport. Now, it is modern, comfortable, and easy to use.
Other airports in New York, like JFK and Newark, also have many domestic flights. Southwest Airlines also flies from LGA. But because LaGuardia Airport mainly does domestic flights and it is so close to the city, it really is the best option if you want something easy and fast. Just remember, traffic can get busy, so it is smart to check how the drive looks, especially when lots of people are on the road.

## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
After you land, you need to get into Manhattan. The good news is that New York has many ways to travel, so you can find what works best for you. There are cheap options like the subway and bus services. There are also airport shuttles that are easy to use. If you want a quick and easy ride, you can pick a taxi or use a rideshare.
No matter if you want to save money and use public transport, want the easy pick of an airport shuttle, or just want the comfort of a private car, you will find something that works. You can get from your gate to your hotel near Grand Central or any other place you want to go. Now, let’s see some good ways to finish your trip in New York.
texts.19:
## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
### Airport Shuttle Services
Airport shuttle services give you a nice way to travel that sits between using public transit and taking a private car. These are vans or buses that you share with other people. This way is easy for you and does not cost much. It gets you from the airport to your hotel or other place in the city. You will usually see these shuttles waiting in special spots outside the baggage claim area.
There are a few companies that run shared shuttle services at JFK, LaGuardia, and Newark. You will be with other people in the shuttle, so there may be many stops. But it is nice that you get dropped off right at your hotel. The Port Authority website can help you by listing which bus services and shuttle companies are allowed to pick you up at each airport.
Here are some key points about airport shuttles:
*   They are not as expensive as a taxi or a private car.  
*   You can often get your spot ahead of time by booking online.  
*   How long the ride takes can change depending on traffic or how many stops there are.  
*   Make sure you use official bus services and go to the main shuttle counters in the airport so you do not get caught in a scam.

## Transportation Options from New York Airports to Manhattan
### Public Transit (Subway, Train, Bus)
Taking public transit is the best way to save money when you travel from New York’s airports to New York City. All three main airports are linked to the city by public transit, but each one is a bit different. This way of getting around works well if you do not have much luggage, and you get to see New York City like people who live here.
If you arrive at JFK, you can ride the AirTrain, and then switch to the subway or Long Island Rail Road (LIRR). For Newark, use the AirTrain, which connects to NJ Transit trains going right to Penn Station. From LaGuardia, you can use city bus services. These will take you to different subway lines that go all over the metropolitan area.
Here is how to use public transit:
*   **JFK:** AirTrain and then take the Subway (A, E, J, Z lines) or switch to LIRR.  
*   **EWR:** AirTrain then use the NJ Transit train straight to Penn Station.  
*   **LGA:** Q70-SBS LaGuardia Link bus, which is free, to subway lines 7, E, F, M, R.

# Why are the Adirondacks not a national park?
SHARE[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.news10.com%2Fnews%2Fnorth-country%2Fwhy-are-the-adirondacks-not-a-national-park%2F&picture=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.news10.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2Fsites%2F64%2F2019%2F10%2Fadirondacks-4174995_960_720.jpg%3Fw%3D900&title=Why%20are%20the%20Adirondacks%20not%20a%20national%20park%3F&description=Created%20in%201892%2C%20the%20Adirondack%20Park%20is%20known%20for%20its%20expansive%20forests%2C%20lakes%2C%20rivers%20and%20outdoor%20recreational%20activities.%20The%20park%20contains%20six%20million%20acres%20and%20is%20the%20largest%20park%20in%20the%20contiguous%20United%20States.%20However%2C%20it%20does%20not%20have%20a%20national%20park%20designation.)[](mailto:?subject=Why%20are%20the%20Adirondacks%20not%20a%20national%20park%3F&body=From%20NEWS10%20ABC%0A%0A%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.news10.com%2Fnews%2Fnorth-country%2Fwhy-are-the-adirondacks-not-a-national-park%2F)

# Why are the Adirondacks not a national park?
KEENE VALLEY, N.Y. (NEWS10) — Created in 1892, the Adirondack Park is known for its expansive forests, lakes, rivers, and outdoor recreational activities. The park contains six million acres and is the largest park in the contiguous United States. However, it does not have a national park designation.
PHOTOS: Spruce Mountain on a cold winter day
The National Park Service is the organization that designates national parks and landmarks. There are a wide array of designations including national preserve, national monument, national memorial, national historic site, national seashore, and national battlefield park. The organization currently has around 19 naming designations.
The National Park System has 423 national places on its register. To be given a national designation, the place needs to meet the following criteria from the National Park Service:
*   Possess nationally significant natural, cultural or recreational resources  
*   Be a suitable and feasible addition to the National Park System  
*   Require direct National Park Service management instead of protection by some other government agency or by the private sector
What do you know about the Adirondacks’ ‘First Wilderness?’
New York State does have sites that are designated as national places but does not have any national parks, such as Yellowstone or Arcadia. National sites in New York State include:
*   Saratoga National Historic Park, Stillwater  
*   Thomas Cole National Historic Site, Catskill  
*   Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site, Hyde Park  
*   Statue of Liberty, National Monument, New York  
*   Fort Stanwix, National Monument, Rome  
*   Harriet Tubman National Historic Park, Auburn  
*   The Appalachian Trail, National Scenic Trail
Report: Over 450 new infestations in Adirondacks in 2021

# Why are the Adirondacks not a national park?
According to the Adirondack Council, the Adirondack Park takes up one-fifth of the state and is nearly three times the size of Yellowstone National Park. The park is a mix of state-owned and private land. More than half of the park is privately owned land, home to 130,000 permanent and 200,000 seasonal residents. The remaining 45% of the land is publicly owned forest preserve, protected as “Forever Wild” by the New York State Constitution since 1894.
Unlike a national park, the Adirondacks have no formal entrances and no entry fee, since it’s not just public land. The same thing goes for Catskill Park. It’s a mix of private and state-owned land, has no entrance fee, and is also protected as “Forever Wild” by the New York State Constitution.
DEC warns of avalanche risk in the Adirondacks
The Adirondacks do not necessarily fit the criteria for a national park designation. Since much of the land is privately-owned, it doesn’t require direct National Park Service management. The public land is also currently managed by state agencies, including the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.
Although the park does contain significant natural or recreational resources, it may not be suitable or feasible for the national park designation. A complete list of national sites can be found on the National Register of Historic Places, located on the National Park Service website.

# Go Finger Lakes - There are no national parks in New York... | Facebook
## Go Finger Lakes's Post
There are no national parks in New York State. There are national monuments, national recreation areas, and national historical parks, but no sprawling national parks that preserve the natural heritage. But there is one national forest here in Central New York — Finger Lakes National Forest. The forest is home to over thirty miles of trails which have a mixture of uses ranging from hiking, mountain biking, skiing, snowshoeing, and horseback riding. National parks are far more restrictive than state parks. The National Park Service generally allows leashed pets in parking areas, campgrounds, picnic areas, and on paved roads, and keeps them off most trails, beaches, and backcountry. ## Taking a dog to a national park
National parks are far more restrictive than state parks. The National Park Service generally allows leashed pets in parking areas, campgrounds, picnic areas, and on paved roads, and keeps them off most trails, beaches, and backcountry. Rules are set site by site, so check the official page for the one you are visiting before you load the car.

texts.11:
# Why are the Adirondacks not a national park?
KEENE VALLEY, N.Y. (NEWS10) — Created in 1892, the Adirondack Park is known for its expansive forests, lakes, rivers, and outdoor recreational activities. The park contains six million acres and is the largest park in the contiguous United States. However, it does not have a national park designation.
PHOTOS: Spruce Mountain on a cold winter day
The National Park Service is the organization that designates national parks and landmarks. There are a wide array of designations including national preserve, national monument, national memorial, national historic site, national seashore, and national battlefield park. The organization currently has around 19 naming designations.
The National Park System has 423 national places on its register. To be given a national designation, the place needs to meet the following criteria from the National Park Service:
*   Possess nationally significant natural, cultural or recreational resources  
*   Be a suitable and feasible addition to the National Park System  
*   Require direct National Park Service management instead of protection by some other government agency or by the private sector
What do you know about the Adirondacks’ ‘First Wilderness?’
New York State does have sites that are designated as national places but does not have any national parks, such as Yellowstone or Arcadia. National sites in New York State include:
*   Saratoga National Historic Park, Stillwater  
*   Thomas Cole National Historic Site, Catskill  
*   Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site, Hyde Park  
*   Statue of Liberty, National Monument, New York  
*   Fort Stanwix, National Monument, Rome  
*   Harriet Tubman National Historic Park, Auburn  
*   The Appalachian Trail, National Scenic Trail
Report: Over 450 new infestations in Adirondacks in 2021
texts.12:
# Why are the Adirondacks not a national park?
According to the Adirondack Council, the Adirondack Park takes up one-fifth of the state and is nearly three times the size of Yellowstone National Park. The park is a mix of state-owned and private land. More than half of the park is privately owned land, home to 130,000 permanent and 200,000 seasonal residents. The remaining 45% of the land is publicly owned forest preserve, protected as “Forever Wild” by the New York State Constitution since 1894.
Unlike a national park, the Adirondacks have no formal entrances and no entry fee, since it’s not just public land. The same thing goes for Catskill Park. It’s a mix of private and state-owned land, has no entrance fee, and is also protected as “Forever Wild” by the New York State Constitution.
DEC warns of avalanche risk in the Adirondacks
The Adirondacks do not necessarily fit the criteria for a national park designation. Since much of the land is privately-owned, it doesn’t require direct National Park Service management. The public land is also currently managed by state agencies, including the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.
Although the park does contain significant natural or recreational resources, it may not be suitable or feasible for the national park designation. A complete list of national sites can be found on the National Register of Historic Places, located on the National Park Service website.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
**Travel Trade Statistics**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Privacy
The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Spending by international visitors to the United States (travel exports) totaled $213.1 billion in 2023, an increase of $47.6 billion (+29%) from $165.5 billion in 2022 to a level 89% of travel exports in 2019. Travel exports accounted for 7.0% of total U.S. exports of goods and services in 2023, up from 5.5% in 2022. Travel exports supported 1.6 million U.S. jobs in 2023 3.
Spending by U.S. residents abroad (travel imports) totaled $215.4 billion in 2023, an increase of $53.5 billion (+33%) from $161.9 billion in 2022 to a level 17% above travel imports in 2019.
Travel yielded a $2.3 billion trade deficit in 2023.
**NTTO Releases New Data Visualization Tool**
NTTO is releasing a Country Profile Monitor, which includes annual visitation, traveler characteristics and economic impact of travel to the United States for 71 countries.
Click hereto see this new tool!
**1 ADIS/I-94 (with stays of 1-night or more in the United States and visiting under certain visa types)**
**2 APIS/ “I-92” (arrivals + departures)**

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.
texts.9:
# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
### Limitations
As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.

### Privacy
The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions.

# NTTO Updates U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor
## TOP U.S. STATES AND CITIES VISITED MONITOR UPDATED TO CALENDAR YEAR 2024
> Top state visited by overseas visitors: New York (9,802,000)  
>   
>   
>   
> Top city-MSA (Metropolitan Statistical Area) visited by overseas visitors: New York City (9,525,000)
The International Trade Administration’s National Travel and Tourism Office (NTTO) has updated its U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor, a data visualization tool highlighting overseas visitation to U.S. states and cities through interactive tables and maps, to calendar year 2024. Highlights for 2024 include:
*   Top state visited by overseas visitors: New York (9,802,000)  
*   Top city-MSA visited by overseas visitors: New York City (9,525,000)  
*   Biggest state # gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Florida (+927,000)  
*   Biggest % gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Vermont (+87.8%)  
*   Top 5 states’ combined market share: 62.0% of overseas visitors  
*   Top 5 city-MSA’s combined market share: 48.5% of overseas visitors
**U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor** has six sections:
*   **Top 5 States and U.S. Cities in 2024**: volume, gains and declines  
*   **Select a U.S. State**: state rank, volume, # change, % change, market share and top cities-MSAs  
*   **Map of Top States-Cities-MSAs**: interactive display of top cities-MSAs visited in each state  
*   **Top U.S. States Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share  
*   **Top U.S. Cities-MSAs Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share  
*   **Download Data**: download data into excel

We need to find which of these have no congressionally designated National Park within borders, and have 3 or fewer international airports.

We need to check for each state:

- National Parks (cong. designated) list. States with no national parks: Many states. The top 10 list includes states that likely have national parks: New York has none; Nevada has some (e.g., Great Basin National Park? Actually Great Basin is in Nevada). Nevada also has Great Basin NP. Texas has Big Bend NP. California has several (Yosemite, Sequoia, etc). Hawaii has Haleakalā, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes, etc. Florida none? Florida has no national parks but has some national sites. Massachusetts none? Actually Massachusetts has no national parks except maybe national memorial sites but not parks. Illinois none? No national parks; maybe there are national memorials. New Jersey none? New Jersey has no national parks. Virginia has Shenandoah NP. So list all those with no NP: New York, Florida, Massachusetts, Illinois, New Jersey, maybe also Hawaii? Hawaii has national parks. So those with no NP among top ten: New York, Florida, Massachusetts, Illinois, New Jersey.

Now airports: Need count of international airports (IATA codes with international flights) in each state. We need 3 or fewer. Let's research each.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of airports in New York State**, grouped by type and sorted by location. It contains all public-use and military airports in the state. Some private-use and former airports may be included where notable, such as airports that were previously public-use, those with commercial enplanements recorded by the FAA or airports assigned an IATA airport code.
This list contains the following information:

*   **City served** – The city generally associated with the airport, as per the airport's master record with the Federal Aviation Administration. This is not always the actual location since some airports are located in smaller towns outside of the city they serve. It is not meant to be a complete list of cities served, which can be found in or added to each airport's Wikipedia article.  
*   **FAA** – The location identifier assigned by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).These are linked to each airport's page at the New York State Department of Transportation.  
*   **IATA** – The airport code assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). Those that do not match the FAA code are shown in bold.  
*   **ICAO** – The location indicator assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).  
*   **Airport name** – The official airport name. Those shown in **bold** indicate the airport has scheduled passenger service on commercial airlines.  
*   **Role** – One of four FAA airport categories, as per the 2021–2025 National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS) report released September 2020:   
    *   P-_s_: _Commercial service – primary_ are publicly owned airports that receive scheduled passenger service and have more than 10,000 passenger boardings (_enplanements_) each year. Each primary airport is sub-classified by the FAA as one of the following four "hub" types (_s_):   
        *   L: _Large hub_ that accounts for at least 1% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   M: _Medium hub_ that accounts for between 0.25% and 1% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   S: _Small hub_ that accounts for between 0.05% and 0.25% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   N: _Nonhub_ that accounts for less than 0.05% of total U.S. passenger enplanements, but more than 10,000 annual enplanements.

    *   CS: _Commercial service – nonprimary_ are publicly owned airports that receive scheduled passenger service and have at least 2,500 passenger boardings each year.  
    *   R: _Reliever_ airports are designated by the FAA to relieve congestion at a large commercial service airport and to provide more general aviation access to the overall community.  
    *   GA: _General aviation_ airports are the largest single group of airports in the U.S. airport system. They are public-use airports that do not have scheduled service or have scheduled service with less than 2,500 passenger boardings each year.

*   **Enplanements** – The number of _enplanements_ (commercial passenger boardings) that occurred at the airport in calendar year 2024, as per FAA records released October 2025.

It is not meant to be a complete list of cities served, which can be found in or added to each airport's Wikipedia article.  
*   **FAA** – The location identifier assigned by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).These are linked to each airport's page at the New York State Department of Transportation.  
*   **IATA** – The airport code assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). Those that do not match the FAA code are shown in bold.  
*   **ICAO** – The location indicator assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).  
*   **Airport name** – The official airport name. Those shown in **bold** indicate the airport has scheduled passenger service on commercial airlines.  
*   **Role** – One of four FAA airport categories, as per the 2021–2025 National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS) report released September 2020:   
    *   P-_s_: _Commercial service – primary_ are publicly owned airports that receive scheduled passenger service and have more than 10,000 passenger boardings (_enplanements_) each year. Each primary airport is sub-classified by the FAA as one of the following four "hub" types (_s_):   
        *   L: _Large hub_ that accounts for at least 1% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   M: _Medium hub_ that accounts for between 0.25% and 1% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   S: _Small hub_ that accounts for between 0.05% and 0.25% of total U.S. passenger enplanements.  
        *   N: _Nonhub_ that accounts for less than 0.05% of total U.S. passenger enplanements, but more than 10,000 annual enplanements.
texts.2:
*   CS: _Commercial service – nonprimary_ are publicly owned airports that receive scheduled passenger service and have at least 2,500 passenger boardings each year.  
    *   R: _Reliever_ airports are designated by the FAA to relieve congestion at a large commercial service airport and to provide more general aviation access to the overall community.  
    *   GA: _General aviation_ airports are the largest single group of airports in the U.S. airport system. They are public-use airports that do not have scheduled service or have scheduled service with less than 2,500 passenger boardings each year.

*   **Enplanements** – The number of _enplanements_ (commercial passenger boardings) that occurred at the airport in calendar year 2024, as per FAA records released October 2025.

Title: How many national parks does MA have? Depends on your definition of 'national park'
Chunks: 0,1,2
June 27, 2025, 5:10 a.m. ET
*   Boston National Historical Park, encompassing portions of Downtown Boston, Charlestown and South Boston, is a national park managed by the National Park Service.  
*   There is a difference between national parks in general, of which there are 429, and parks with the National Park designation, of which there are 63.  
*   NPS manages 18 recreational spaces in Massachusetts, including national historical parks, national scenic trails, national seashores, national recreation areas and national historic sites.
Did you know Boston is anational park?
It may not have the grand vistas of theGrand Canyonor the jaw dropping sight ofOld Faithfulerupting, but Boston National Historical Park, which encompasses portions of Downtown Boston, Charlestown and South Boston, is a national park managed by the National Park Service.
It’sone of 18national parks in Massachusetts – but there are no parks with a National Park designation in the state.
Confused? Here’s an explanation.

## What is a National Park?
As a primer, let’s talk about the difference between national parks in general, of which there are 429, and parks with the National Park designation, of which there are 63.
The National Park System uses nearly 20 different naming conventions for the different recreational spaces they manage. There are national historical parks, national seashores, national historic sites and national monuments, just to name a few of them.
All of them can be called “parks,” according to the National Park System.
A National Park is a specific designation.
“Generally, a national park contains a variety of resources and encompasses large land or water areas to help provide adequate protection of the resources,” the National Park System wrote in a post explaining the different names. For a sense of how large, more than 10 national parks are largerthan the state of Rhode Island.
Massachusetts doesn’t have any parks that fall under this designation, but it does have 18 parks under NPS.

## What are Massachusetts’s national parks?
NPS manages 18 recreational spaces in Massachusetts, including national historical parks, national scenic trails, national seashores, national recreation areas and national historic sites.
Here’s a list:
*   Adams: National Historical Park  
*   Appalachian: National Scenic Trail  
*   Blackstone River Valley: National Historical Park  
*   Boston: National Historical Park  
*   Boston African American: National Historic Site  
*   Boston Harbor Islands: National Recreation Area  
*   Cape Cod: National Seashore  
*   Frederick Law Olmsted: National Historic Site  
*   John Fitzgerald Kennedy: National Historic Site  
*   Longfellow House Washington's Headquarters: National Historic Site  
*   Lowell: National Historical Park  
*   Minute Man: National Historical Park  
*   New Bedford Whaling: National Historical Park  
*   New England: National Scenic Trail  
*   Salem Maritime: National Historic Site  
*   Saugus Iron Works: National Historic Site  
*   Springfield Armory: National Historic Site  
*   Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route: National Historic Trail

Massachusetts has no designated U.S. national park. The closest of the 63 by straight-line distance from the state center is Acadia (about 233 miles). Cape Cod National Seashore is the in-state NPS landscape most visitors already know, but it is a seashore, not a national park.

## How to choose from here
Acadia is the national park Massachusetts searches and drives to. Cape Cod National Seashore is the in-state coastal unit most people already know; it is a seashore. Shenandoah is only the better pick if the trip is already aimed at Virginia.

### Acadia National Park

Fee:$35 per vehicle (7 days)
Camping:4 campgrounds
Dogs:Acadia is one of the more pet-friendly national parks: leashed pets are allowed on most hiking trails and all 45 miles of carriage roads, and in Blackwoods, Seawall, and Schoodic Woods campgrounds. Several ladder/cliff trails and seasonal beaches are closed to pets.

## Driving to a national park from Massachusetts cities
### Shenandoah National Park
Just 75 miles from the bustle of Washington, D.C., Shenandoah National Park is a land bursting with cascading waterfalls, spectacular vistas, fields of wildflowers, and quiet wooded hollows. With over 200,000 acres of protected lands that are haven to deer,…
Fee:$30 per vehicle (7 days)
Camping:4 campgrounds
Dogs:Shenandoah is one of the few national parks that allow leashed pets on most of its 500+ miles of trails, plus campgrounds and some lodging. A short list of trails is closed to pets (including Old Rag routes, Dark Hollow Falls, Stony Man, Limberlost, Bearfence, and a few others).
Fees, camping & pet rules →
508 miles straight-line from the center of Massachusetts

Fee:Free entry

Dogs:New River Gorge allows pets on all trails if they stay on a 6-foot physical leash. Pets are not allowed in park buildings, visitor centers, or ranger-led programs.
Fees, camping & pet rules →

### Congaree National Park
Astonishing biodiversity exists in Congaree National Park, the largest intact expanse of old growth bottomland hardwood forest remaining in the southeastern United States. Waters from the Congaree and Wateree Rivers sweep through the floodplain, carrying nu…
Fee:Free entry
Camping:2 campgrounds
Dogs:Congaree is unusually pet-friendly: leashed pets are allowed on all trails, including the boardwalk, and in campgrounds. Bring water in summer heat and humidity.
Fees, camping & pet rules →

## NPS sites in Massachusetts that are not national parks
Massachusetts NPS sites include Cape Cod National Seashore and Boston National Historical Park. They are not among the 63 national parks.

## FAQ: parks near Massachusetts
›Does Massachusetts have a national park?  
No. Massachusetts is not home to any of the 63 designated U.S. national parks. Massachusetts NPS sites include Cape Cod National Seashore and Boston National Historical Park. They are not among the 63 national parks.
›What is the closest national park to Massachusetts?  
Acadia National Park, about 233 miles straight-line from the geographic center of Massachusetts — not driving distance from a specific city.
›What is the closest national park to Boston?  
From Boston, the closest national park by car is Acadia National Park: about 249 road miles, 4–5½ hours without traffic to Acadia Gateway Center. Next is Shenandoah (512 miles, 8½–11 hours).
›Which nearby national park should I pick from Massachusetts?  
Acadia is the national park Massachusetts searches and drives to. Cape Cod National Seashore is the in-state coastal unit most people already know; it is a seashore. Shenandoah is only the better pick if the trip is already aimed at Virginia.
›When is the best time to visit parks near Massachusetts?  
June to early October for Acadia. Cape Cod's shoulder seasons (June and September) are less crowded than July and August.
›Are dogs allowed at those nearby parks?  
Rules vary. Most national parks allow leashed pets only in developed areas, not on trails. Open each park page for the official rule.

## FAQ: parks near Massachusetts
›Does Massachusetts have a national park?  
No. Massachusetts is not home to any of the 63 designated U.S. national parks. Massachusetts NPS sites include Cape Cod National Seashore and Boston National Historical Park. They are not among the 63 national parks.
›What is the closest national park to Massachusetts?  
Acadia National Park, about 233 miles straight-line from the geographic center of Massachusetts — not driving distance from a specific city.
›What is the closest national park to Boston?  
From Boston, the closest national park by car is Acadia National Park: about 249 road miles, 4–5½ hours without traffic to Acadia Gateway Center. Next is Shenandoah (512 miles, 8½–11 hours).
›Which nearby national park should I pick from Massachusetts?  
Acadia is the national park Massachusetts searches and drives to. Cape Cod National Seashore is the in-state coastal unit most people already know; it is a seashore. Shenandoah is only the better pick if the trip is already aimed at Virginia.
›When is the best time to visit parks near Massachusetts?  
June to early October for Acadia. Cape Cod's shoulder seasons (June and September) are less crowded than July and August.
›Are dogs allowed at those nearby parks?  
Rules vary. Most national parks allow leashed pets only in developed areas, not on trails. Open each park page for the official rule.
